rows.title: [Feature] Add search pets by name screen
rows.excerpt:
## Summary

Add a new screen that allows users to search for pets by name, similar to the existing "Find Owners" functionality.

## Motivation

- Currently there is no way to search for a pet directly by name; users must first find the owner and then browse their pets.
- A dedicated pet search screen would improve usability when the pet name is known but the owner is not.
- Aligns the pet entity with the same search UX pattern already established for owners.

## Proposed Solution

1. **New Thymeleaf template** (`templates/pets/findPets.html`) with a search form and results list/table.
2. **New controller** endpoint(s) in a `PetController` (or extend existing controller) to handle `GET /pets/find` and `GET /pets` with a `name` query parameter.
3. **New repository method** `findByNameContainingIgnoreCase(String name)` (or equivalent Spring Data query) in `PetRepository`.
4. **Navigation link** added to the main layout so users can access the pet search screen.
5. **Accessibility**: the new page must meet WCAG 2.2 Level AA (keyboard navigation, visible focus, proper labels, contrast, landmarks, etc.).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A "Find Pets" link is available in the main navigation menu
- [ ] Users can search for pets by entering a full or partial pet name (case-insensitive)
- [ ] An empty search returns all pets
- [ ] Search results display pet name, birth date, type, and owner name
- [ ] Clicking a result navigates to the pet's or owner's detail page
- [ ] The page is accessible (landmarks, labels, keyboard support, contrast)
- [ ] Unit and integration tests cover the new controller and repository methods
- [ ] Works with H2 (default), MySQL, and PostgreSQL profiles

## Alternatives Considered

- Extending the existing owner search to also filter by pet name — rejected because it conflates two different search intents.

## Additional Context

The implementation should follow the same patterns used by the existing "Find Owners" feature (`OwnerController`, `findOwners.html`, `ownersList.html`).

rows.title: Owner.addPet silently ignores persisted pets and PetValidator lacks name length check
rows.excerpt:
The Owner.addPet(Pet pet) method in Owner.java contains a logic bug where it only adds a pet to the owner's pet list if pet.isNew() returns true (i.e., the pet has no ID). This means that any persisted pet (one that already has a database ID assigned) is silently ignored when added to an owner.

This bug manifests in PetController.updatePetDetails() where the else branch calls owner.addPet(pet) for a pet with an existing ID. Since the pet is not new, the call silently does nothing, and the pet is never associated with the owner.

Expected behavior: The addPet method should add any pet that is not already present in the owner's pet list, regardless of whether the pet is new or persisted.

Actual behavior: Only pets with a null ID are added. Pets with a valid ID are silently dropped.

Additionally, the PetValidator class lacks a name length validation check. The Pet entity inherits from NamedEntity which has a @Column(length=30) constraint, but the validator does not enforce this at the form validation level. This means names exceeding 30 characters pass validation but fail at the database level with a hard-to-debug constraint violation.

Steps to reproduce:

Create an Owner instance
Create a Pet instance and assign it an ID (e.g., pet.setId(5))
Call owner.addPet(pet)
Observe that owner.getPets() returns an empty list
Acceptance criteria:

Owner.addPet adds persisted pets that are not already in the list
Owner.addPet does not add duplicate pets
PetValidator rejects pet names longer than 30 characters
All existing tests continue to pass
New unit tests cover the fixed behavior
Word count: ~240 RULE 7 status: PASS

### 2. `PetController.initCreationForm`

Three related removals:

- **`ModelMap model` parameter** - declared but never referenced.
- **`Pet pet = new Pet(); owner.addPet(pet);`** - constructed a transient Pet that was never returned, never persisted (this is a `GET` handler that does not call `owners.save(...)`), and never reached the view (the `pet` model attribute is supplied by the `@ModelAttribute("pet") findPet(...)` method, which constructs its own `new Pet()`). The mutation therefore had no observable effect.
- **`Owner owner` parameter** - with the body emptied, this parameter is no longer referenced either. Spring still resolves the `owner` model attribute through `@ModelAttribute("owner") findOwner(...)`, so the view receives the same data.
- **`org.springframework.ui.ModelMap` import** - now unused following the parameter removal.

## Verification

`./mvnw test` passes unchanged. No tests were modified.

## Review checklist

- [ ] No surviving references to the deleted local `vets` variable in
      `VetController`.
- [ ] No surviving references to the deleted `ModelMap model` or
      `Owner owner` parameters in `PetController.initCreationForm`.
- [ ] `org.springframework.ui.ModelMap` import removed from
      `PetController`.
- [ ] Existing tests pass without modification.

rows.title: Validate owner address and city length to match the database schema
rows.excerpt:
as constrain them to `VARCHAR(255)` and `VARCHAR(80)`. Submitting a longer value through the create-owner form persisted past bean validation and failed with HTTP 500 (`DataIntegrityViolationException: Value too long for column ...`).

This follows the same pattern already used for person names and pet names:

- #2350 (`@Size` on `Person.firstName` / `lastName`)
- #2611 (pet name length aligned with the 30-character column)

`@Size` is added on `Owner.address` (max 255) and `Owner.city` (max 80) so the form returns field errors instead of a 500. No schema or UI changes.

Open PR #2663 covers `Visit.description` only; it does not include these owner columns.

## Reproduction (before)

1. Run the app (`./mvnw spring-boot:run`) and open `http://localhost:8080/owners/new`
2. Fill valid first name, last name, telephone, and a short address
3. Set **City** to 81 characters and submit → HTTP 500, `Value too long for column "CITY CHARACTER VARYING(80)"`
4. Repeat with **Address** of 256 characters → HTTP 500, `Value too long for column "ADDRESS CHARACTER VARYING(255)"`

## Test plan

- [x] `./mvnw -Dtest=OwnerControllerTests test`
- [x] POST `/owners/new` with an 81-character city stays on the form (HTTP 200) with a `Size` field error on `city`
- [x] POST `/owners/new` with a 256-character address stays on the form (HTTP 200) with a `Size` field error on `address`
- [x] Existing owner create/update tests still pass
- [x] Manual check on `/owners/new`: oversized city/address show the inline validation message and no longer hit the error page

rows.title: Delete functionality for Owners
rows.excerpt: Description: - Adds the ability to delete an Owner from the Owner details page, along with all associated Pets and Visits (cascade delete). Changes: - Added deleteOwner() handler in OwnerController (POST /owners/{ownerId}/delete) - Added delete(Owner) to OwnerRepository - Added "Delete Owner" button to ownerDetails.html, with a JS confirm dialog to prevent accidental deletion - Cascade delete relies on existing CascadeType.ALL mapping on Owner.pets and Pet.visits - Added Javadoc comments for the new controller method and repository method Tests: - Verified successful delete redirects to /owners/find with a flash success message - Verified the correct Owner (with pets) is passed to delete() - Verified deleting a non-existent owner throws/returns an error, and delete() is never called - Verified GET on the delete endpoint is rejected (405)
